title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any director (as defined in AASB 124).

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board; when the Chairman wishes to trade, approval must instead come from the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Directors and executives
tiers.description: A subset of Key Management Personnel additionally excluded from dealing between receipt of the Board Pack and the Directors' Meeting, and subject to the ASX relevant-interest notification obligation.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of Directors and employees, such as family members, family trusts and family companies, as well as customers and suppliers; the approval obligation applies to their trading as well as to the Key Management Person's own dealings.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holdings in the Company

windows.start_anchor: 14 days prior to the release of annual, half yearly or quarterly results
14 days prior to the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Dealing is also prohibited at any time price sensitive information exists that has not been disclosed because of an ASX Listing Rule disclosure exception; the Policy does not name a specific person with authority to impose this or state whether it is confidential.

rules.detail: 'Securities' expressly includes derivatives related to the Company's shares whether issued by the Company or not, so a bank-written OTC put/call is covered; dealing in it requires prior written approval from the Chairman (or Chair of the Audit Committee) and must sit outside Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: This Policy covers trading in shares in the Company, derivatives related to the Company's shares, whether issued by the Company or not and to any traded Company options.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on derivatives over unvested securities, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging that limits the economic risk of unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration scheme, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Hedging or otherwise limiting economic risk of vested holdings (which would include a collar) requires prior written clearance via the Approval Process (Chairman or Chair of the Audit Committee) before entry.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holdings in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance in accordance with the Approval Process.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure limits economic risk of the holding and so falls within the same clearance requirement as hedging.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holdings in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance in accordance with the Approval Process.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. Ordinary buying or selling is only restricted by the Blackout Periods and the insider-trading prohibition; there is no separate ban or clearance regime for short sales specifically.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not deal in securities of the Company within the following periods.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named specifically but fall within 'derivatives related to the Company's shares, whether issued by the Company or not', triggering the same clearance requirement as other derivatives.
rules.evidence: derivatives related to the Company's shares, whether issued by the Company or not

rules.detail: A margin loan is expressly permitted with prior written approval from the Chairman (or Chair of the Audit Committee), on disclosure of the number of securities, key terms and trigger points, and the lender's rights to sell.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel intending to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that the company's securities may be traded pursuant to the terms of a margin loan must obtain prior written approval from the Chairman or in his absence the Chairman of the Audit Committee.

rules.detail: Granting a lender rights over the security holding (e.g. a charge securing the collar loan) is expressly permitted with prior written clearance via the Approval Process.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel must not enter into arrangements that provide lenders with rights over their security holdings in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance in accordance with the Approval Process.

rules.detail: 'Other financing arrangement' beyond margin loans is expressly captured and permitted with the same prior written Chairman/Audit Committee approval and disclosure of terms.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel intending to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that the company's securities may be traded pursuant to the terms of a margin loan must obtain prior written approval from the Chairman or in his absence the Chairman of the Audit Committee.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or short-term dealing restriction is stated.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or in his absence, the Chair of the Audit Committee)
clearance.section: Approval Process; Margin Loans; Prohibited Transactions
clearance.evidence: Contact the Chairman, or in his absence the Chair of the Audit Committee, and notified them of their intention to trade in the Company's securities and obtained prior written approval
Where the Chairman wishes to trade in securities, he must contact the Chair of the Audit Committee and notify them of their intention to trade and obtained their prior written approval.
Directors must notify the Company Secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the company.

exceptions.evidence: Transfers of existing securities into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in Key Management Personnel are a beneficiary
An investment in, or trading of, a fund or scheme (other than a scheme solely investing in the Company's securities) where the assets are invested at the discretion of a third party
Undertakings to accept or the acceptance of a takeover offer
Trading under an offer or initiation made to all or most of the security holders such as a rights issue, security purchase plan, dividend reinvestment plan and an equal access buyback
A disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their security rights for example under a margin lending arrangement.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or Chair of the Audit Committee)
exceptions.evidence: Satisfy the Chairman that the person seeking clearance is in severe financial hardship or trading is required in compliance with a court order or other legal or regulatory requirement.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or Chair of the Audit Committee)
exceptions.evidence: Satisfy the Chairman that the person seeking clearance ... is in severe financial hardship or trading is required in compliance with a court order or other legal or regulatory requirement.

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel; trigger: inception of a margin loan or other financing arrangement where the Company's securities risk being traded under its terms; to whom: Chairman (or in his absence, Chair of the Audit Committee); deadline: before entering into the arrangement (prior written approval), disclosing the number of securities involved, key terms and trigger points, and the lender's rights to sell.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit Committee) may approve trading within a Blackout Period only where the person is not in possession of price sensitive information and is in severe financial hardship or trading is required by a court order or other legal/regulatory requirement; confidentiality of the approval is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman must be informed of the following information when applying for written approval for a margin loan: a) the number of the Company's securities involved; b) key terms and trigger points of the margin loan; c) the rights of the lender to sell securities; and d) any other material information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's secured loan against the collared shares must be disclosed to the Chairman in detail (size, terms, trigger points, and the bank's enforcement rights) before the executive may proceed, giving the company visibility into, and an effective gate over, the collar's economic terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy covers trading in shares in the Company, derivatives related to the Company's shares, whether issued by the Company or not and to any traded Company options.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves covered 'securities' regardless of who issues them, so the whole collar structure (not just any share transfer) requires the Chairman's prior written clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel must not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested securities. ... Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no clearance route around this: a funded collar can only be written over already-vested Focus Minerals shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their security rights for example under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from this policy]. Even if trading is excluded from this Policy, Key Management Personnel must not trade in the Company's securities if they are possession of insider information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is excluded from the Policy altogether (including during Blackout Periods), which is favourable for the loan leg, though the KMP-level insider information caveat is preserved as a residual risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and executives are also excluded from dealing in securities within the period from receipt of the Board Pack and the Directors' Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This recurring, unscheduled blackout (tied to board cycle rather than calendar dates) further narrows the windows available to enter, adjust or unwind the collar.

summary: A funded collar is achievable for a FML Key Management Person over vested shares, but requires proactive Chairman-level clearance and cannot be written over unvested equity incentives. 'Securities' expressly includes third-party (OTC) derivatives over the Company's shares, and separate provisions require prior written approval from the Chairman (or Chair of the Audit Committee) for any arrangement limiting economic risk (hedging), any arrangement giving a lender rights over the holding (encumbrance), and any margin loan or 'other financing arrangement' risking the securities being traded, with mandatory disclosure of the number of securities, key terms and trigger points, and the lender's rights to sell. Derivatives and hedging over unvested securities are banned outright with no clearance route. Entry, adjustment and unwind must fall outside the 14-day pre-results/AGM blackouts (plus a 1-hour post-results wait) and the Directors'/executives' Board Pack blackout, and while the KMP holds no inside information; helpfully, a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Policy entirely, including during Blackout Periods. Overall, the structure is workable subject to the company being given full visibility of, and a clearance opportunity over, both the derivative and secured-loan legs before execution.
